description: Half a shell lined in green and gold fire. Dunedelver turns them up from a sea that dried out long ago.
lore: The inside of one does the northern sky when a fire catches it: green sheeting into gold, then gone, then back a little to the left. People notice. People have always noticed, and the dune camps have priced accordingly.

Who buys them is the part worth writing down. It is the ones left behind by [[lore/the_long_morning|the Long Morning]] — the sister, the man whose friend of four hundred years was simply not in the room one evening — and they are not fooled, and will say so before you can raise it. It is a shell. It is not that light. They buy it anyway and set it where they will catch it by accident, on a sill, beside a door, because a thing that ambushes you with that colour twice a week is as near as they can get to being reminded of somebody they cannot manage to miss.
gm_notes: The missing grief seen from a shop counter: people bereaved by the Long Morning buying a colour on purpose, because the sorrow will not arrive by itself. Advances nothing — it only puts the phenomenon in a player's hand at seventy-five gold.
